items.title: 'Had to do something': As auction clearance rates drop PM defends policy
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese issues an impassioned defence of CGT changes from the budget and Australia's multicultural society.

items.title: Bondi terror attack survivor received 'influx of hate' hours after shooting
items.description: Deepfake and altered images depicting a Bondi Beach terror attack survivor holding an Academy Award while covered in blood spread "like wildfire" online just hours after the shooting, a royal commission has heard.

items.title: MP says she misunderstood meaning of 'headlock' when making allegation
items.description: State Liberal MP Moira Deeming says she misunderstood the meaning of the term "headlock", after alleging her party room colleague Matthew Guy assaulted her.

items.title: The lucrative business of super switching is ringing alarm bells
items.description: There is now more than $1 trillion in self-managed superannuation funds, which means a big chunk of money isn't regulated by APRA, and it's the rate of the shift into SMSFs and less-regulated managed investment schemes that has regulators worried.

items.title: Vanuatu critical infrastructure to remain 'free from militarisation' under pact
items.description: Vanuatu's Prime Minister Jotham Napat and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ink the Nakamal Agreement, almost 10 months after Mr Napat pulled out of a planned signing ceremony in Port Vila, citing concerns around sovereignty.

items.title: 'I've got all the symptoms': Matty Robbins was a hero of the AFL. Now he's suffering
items.description: More than 30 professional and amateur Aussie Rules players have been diagnosed with CTE, revealing that the brain trauma crisis is striking all levels of the game.

items.title: 'Terrible tragedy': Minister won't request coronial inquest into baby's death
items.description: WA's health minister says she would support a coronial inquest into the death of an eight-month-old girl at Kalgoorlie Health Campus, but says it is a decision for the state coroner.

items.title: Alleged Russian spies charged with new espionage offence
items.description: Crown prosecutors presented a new bench charge for the couple of conspiracy to commit espionage.

items.title: Bronze tugboat propellers worth $2m stolen in WA's north
items.description: In a heist not seen before in this WA mining town, thieves have allegedly made away with eight tonnes of tugboat propellers, with the copper estimated to be worth an eye-watering $2 million.

items.title: ICAC hears uni executive sacked the day he rejected colleague's pay rise
items.description: The ICAC inquiry has heard a former University of Wollongong executive was dismissed on the day of a disputed salary increase.

items.title: Woman feared 'being sent to hell' if she escaped cult, court told
items.description: An alleged victim of cult leader William "Little Pebble" Kamm has told a court she began experiencing extreme anxiety as she pondered an escape from a property on the NSW South Coast.

items.title: Jillaroos, jackaroos and an iconic event: The Brunette Races in pictures
items.description: More than 800 people from across northern Australia hit a remote outback cattle station over the weekend for the iconic annual Brunette Races.

items.title: Bruce Lehrmann loses legal bid for Brittany Higgins documentary footage
items.description: Former Liberal staffer Bruce Lehrmann has been knocked back in a bid to gain access to raw documentary footage which featured Brittany Higgins.

items.title: Surgeon sounded 'exhausted' a week before fatal crash, brother says
items.description: The brother of Royal Hobart Hospital doctor Artyom Avetisyan says the cardiothoracic surgery registrar sounded "extremely exhausted" in the week before his crash death.

items.title: Lauryn Hill credited with reshaping music and inspiring generations
items.description: American musician and actress Lauryn Hill has been recognised with the inaugural Living Legend Icon Award at the BET Awards by the Black Entertainment Television network in the United States.

items.title: Four ways to turn tinned chickpeas into a delicious dinner
items.description: From comforting curry to hearty soup, these easy recipes will get chickpeas out of the pantry and onto the menu.

items.title: Outback town set to star in new thriller as film festival kicks off
items.description: Red Dog director Kriv Stenders reveals plans for a new thriller film as the annual Vision Splendid Outback Film Festival kicks off in Winton.

items.title: NASA to bump telescope back into space to avoid it falling to Earth
items.description: US space agency NASA is racing to save an aging telescope, used to observe cosmic explosions, from falling back to Earth with a daring rescue mission.

items.title: How a handshake may decide Slater's Maroons coaching future
items.description: Billy Slater says he will not sign another contract to be Queensland State of Origin coach, but that does not mean he will not continue in the role.

items.title: Ben Stokes's retirement a perfect example of his main character energy
items.description: Ben Stokes has been the centre of England's cricketing universe for 15 years. In announcing his retirement mid-match, he highlighted how damaging that main character energy can be.

items.title: Les Mills, NZ Olympian and founder of global fitness brand, dies aged 91
items.description: The New Zealand Olympian who opened an Auckland gym in 1968 that grew into an international group fitness brand has died aged 91.

items.title: Teen charged twice in three days over alleged stolen car pursuits
items.description: A 14-year-old boy charged twice in three days after allegedly leading police on stolen car pursuits is among several incidents prompting the police union to call for tougher bail laws in the ACT.

items.title: Allan government under pressure amid latest Big Build corruption allegations
items.description: The Victorian premier has backed her government's response to corruption in the construction industry, despite criticism from across politics and integrity experts.

items.title: France records 1,000 excess daily deaths as record heatwave broken by severe storms
items.description: More than 150 million Europeans swelter in "extreme heat", which scientists say has been the worst the continent has ever recorded.

items.title: Network 10 strikes last-minute deal to extend broadcasting in SA and NSW
items.description: Two regions in South Australia and one in New South Wales were set to lose access to free-to-air Network 10 services in coming days, but a new agreement means coverage will continue until the end of September.
